UCF vs Iowa State prediction Beating Iowa State is pretty simple: Contain Aiden Flora, and you've got 'em. The third-year sophomore has five games in which he's gone over 100 yards. In those games, his lowest output was 182 yards in a 42-31 defense-optional shootout against Baylor two weeks ago. The Cyclones are 4-0 in those other games, three of which saw Flora surpass 200 yards on the ground. He's racked up a ridiculous 619 yards and six touchdowns over the past three games, adding eight catches for 58 yards as well as a pair of pass completions (only one went for anything, a 37-yarder last week vs. Cincinnati). UCF's run defense ranks eighth in the 16-team Big 12 at just under 137 yards per game. They held Arizona State to 3.6 yards per carry last week but surrendered nearly 5 ypc and four touchdowns to Kansas in a winning effort the week prior. Arkansas State transfer Jaylen Raynor has led the Big 12's worst passing offense at just under 207 yards per game, but even he's played better in recent weeks amid Flora's ascension, throwing for 794 yards and six TDs against just two interceptions. The Knights can absolutely win on Senior Night. The run game was stifled by Arizona State, but UCF was without lead back Duke Watson, and Iowa State has the third-worst run-stopping unit in the Big 12. If everyone is back and healthy, and if Alonza Barnett can complement that with some timely strikes, the Knights can get the win. The Cyclones haven't won any of their four road games this season, but three of those teams (Iowa, BYU and Arizona) are ranked. A bowl berth might come down to the final week, just like it did in 2023. picks.blurb: 2026 Week 12 Preview: Iowa State Cyclones @ UCF Knights | Underdog Dynasty Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Rest of the FBS Community Underdog Dynasty November 19, 2026 Underdog Dynasty Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Conference USA Sun Belt Conference American Athletic Conference Betting FanDuel College Football Odds College Football Picks and Predictions Community Guidelines Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Conference USA Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds All communities Notifications Big 12 UCF and Iowa State battle for bowl eligibility at the Bounce House, while Aiden Flora is on a hot streak. Time and date: Friday, November 20 at 6:00 p.m. ET Location: Acrisure Bounce House — Orlando, FL Spread: UCF (-2.5) Over/under: 49.5 All-time series: Iowa State leads, 1-0 Last meeting: Iowa State 38, UCF 35 — October 19, 2024 Current streak: Iowa State, 1 (2024) Setting the scene Friday night football kicks off early this week. At 6 p.m. ET, the Bounce House welcomes Iowa State for the first time as two 5-5 Big 12 opponents compete for bowl eligibility. UCF has been the master of chaotic finishes this season, recently shocking BYU in double overtime and upending Kansas with a game-winning touchdown on the final snap. Iowa State has also escaped a handful of close finishes this year, sliding past West Virginia in a back-and-forth finish before kicking a game-winning field goal on Halloween to upset Oklahoma State. With two teams accustomed to close finishes chasing that coveted sixth win, and a potential Heisman finisher involved, Friday night in Orlando should feature no shortage of drama. Iowa State Cyclones outlook Iowa State (5-5, 3-4 Big 12) has been as battle-tested as anyone in college football this season. The Cyclones already faced four teams ranked in the top 20 of the latest College Football Playoff rankings. They’ve also defeated three Big 12 opponents with records of 5-5 or greater, eking out close wins over West Virginia and Oklahoma State before blowing the doors of Cincinnati last Saturday. There have been two different versions of the Cyclones in year one under Jimmy Rogers. In Ames, Iowa State is a force to be reckoned with, posting a 5-1 home record with a lone defeat to No. 2 Utah. Yet, the Cyclones remain in search of their first road victory under Rogers, although all four of their road opponents are currently 6-4 or better. Iowa State’s success is largely correlated with the performance of Doak Walker Award semifinalist Aiden Flora. The running back has catapulted into the No. 1 spot on the nation’s rushing leaderboard at 1,335 yards, thanks to three consecutive 180+ yard explosions. Flora has an FBS-best five 180-yard games this year, including three performances where he eclipsed 210 yards. The versatile sophomore is a touchdown machine, and his scoring ability isn’t limited to just the run game. In addition to producing 12 rushing touchdowns, Flora has thrown two passing touchdowns and recorded a punt return touchdown, and he also ranks second on the team in receptions. The explosive Flora has four 60-yard runs this year, a total topped by just three FBS programs. His ability opens up things for the passing game, which has a commensalistic relationship with the future All-Big 12 running back. All three of Jaylen Raynor’s 250-yard showings through the air occurred when Flora crossed 180 on the ground. The mobile quarterback has been able to stretch the field more vertically as of late. He has started 10 games this season, yet 42 percent of his passing yards and 46 percent of his passing touchdowns occurred in the last three weeks. Raynor has established a strong connection with true freshman Jamal Polite Jr., who averages 19.5 yards per reception as the premier downfield threat. But what happens when Flora goes under 180? Iowa State has struggled when it gets behind the sticks. The Cyclones are 113th nationally in third down offense, and Iowa State has converted just 20-of-71 (28.2 percent) third downs across its five losses. The Cyclones have been inconsistent on defense. They enjoyed strong performances against BYU and Cincinnati but allowed at least 39 points in four of their last six contests. Iowa State ranks 108th in total defense, struggling particularly against the run where it allows 174 yards per game on a 4.93 average. Inside linebacker Sullivan Schlimgen has been one of the unit’s key playmakers, checking in at third in the Big 12 with 93 tackles. However, the Cyclones are severely lacking in two categories on defense: sacks and interceptions. They rank 100th in the FBS with 1.6 sacks per game, and defensive end Isaac Terrell leads the unit with 3.5 — producing three of those sacks in the Sept. 5 opener. Additionally, Iowa State has only picked off two passes all season, and two were courtesy of middle linebacker Beau Goodwin. Thus, the secondary looks to make more havoc plays and avoid these high-scoring shootout style games moving forward. UCF Knights outlook UCF (5-5, 3-4 Big 12) is on the brink of its second bowl appearance since joining the Big 12 in 2023. The Knights are the last remaining program that has yet to produce a winning record as a member of the conference, but the opportunity to end the drought presents itself this November. Since stunning then-No. 2 BYU in overtime on Oct. 24, the Knights are 0-2 at home, dropping lopsided contests to Baylor and Arizona State. All four of UCF’s Big 12 losses came by at least 10 points, while all three wins were by single-digits, as the Knights have shown the ability to prosper in tightly-contested games. To qualify for bowl eligibility, UCF must jumpstart its offense which has scored 22 points across its last two games at the Bounce House. The Knights recently returned to their original starting quarterback Alonza Barnett III, who suffered a hamstring injury in Week 2 at Pittsburgh. Barnett has won 13 of his last 16 starts, and the senior has elevated the passing attack, surpassing 250 passing yards in both starts this November. Barnett’s presence on the field has turned wide receiver Josh Derry into a budding star. In his past two games, Derry has hauled in 15 receptions for 280 yards and a touchdown, emerging as the top receiver in this offense. True freshman Tyren Hornes is also making strides, registering 59 receiving yards (his second-highest total of the season) and his second career touchdown against the Sun Devils. However, the Knights must improve their pass protection, as they rank 113th nationally with 2.7 sacks allowed per game. That correlates to an unsatisfying third down conversion rate of 34.4 percent, which sits one spot below Iowa State on the national leaderboard. But perhaps the greatest struggle for UCF’s offense — which is also related to the offensive line — is the decline of the run game. The Knights haven’t produced a 100-yard rusher since Week 3, or a 60-yard rusher in each of their last three games. No UCF running back has rattled off a 20-yard run since Oct. 24, and the Knights look to create lanes for Duke Watson, Landen Chambers, and Taevion Swint to break that streak. The Knights are typically strong starters on defense, and they have yet to allow more than seven points in a first quarter this season. However, finishing games is a priority for a unit that allowed 25 unanswered in the final 20 minutes against Kansas and 27 unanswered in the final 20 minutes against Houston. UCF continues to operate without one of its top defenders in strong safety Demari Henderson, who suffered an injury late in the BYU game on Oct. 24. Still, there is veteran talent across the secondary including cornerback Antione Jackson, whose 10 pass breakups lead the Big 12, and cornerback Jayden Williams, who ranks second on the team with 53 tackles, in addition to recording one interception and two forced fumbles. While the Knights are better than the Cyclones in turnover production, they similarly struggle in getting to opposing quarterbacks. Defensive end Isaiah Nixon leads UCF with 2.5 sacks on the season, and the team has gone consecutive weeks without registering a sack. Despite the offenses trending in different directions, UCF opens as a slight favorite over Iowa State, largely due to the location of the game. The Knights recorded two of their three Big 12 wins at the Bounce House, while the Cyclones have been futile away from home this year. The plamayking of Aiden Flora will be the main determinant in this matchup. Flora recorded over 100 rushing yards and three touchdowns in the first quarter last week, almost single-handedly putting Cincinnati away in 15 minutes. UCF’s defense must be prepared to counter the running back in any way possible. Stacking the box isn’t always an ideal strategy, because Iowa State loves to catch defenses off-guard with his pop passes. The Cyclones will keep things creative on offense, and UCF must remain disciplined defensively beyond the first quarter. Iowa State sustains its offensive rhythm from the last three weeks, while the Knights struggle to find openings for their run game. The end result: the Cyclones become bowl eligible in Jimmy Rogers’ debut season. The Knights are 1.5-point home favorites in a matchup between two teams looking to secure bowl eligibility. Iowa State enters the game following a dominant 41-13 victory over Cincinnati, led by Aiden Flora's 216 rushing yards and three touchdowns. Meanwhile, UCF is coming off a disappointing 26-13 loss to Arizona State. The Cyclones have struggled away from home this season, while the Knights have been much more competitive in Orlando. Kickoff is scheduled for 5:00 p.m. CT on FS1. Below, we'll break down the latest Iowa State vs. UCF odds, where to watch, key injuries and expected starters, along with our prediction and pick for this Friday night Big 12 showdown. Iowa State vs. UCF Odds Spread: UCF -1.5 Over/Under: 54.5 points Moneyline: UCF -112 | Iowa State -108 Odds reported November 15, 2026. Lines subject to change. Where to Watch Iowa State vs. UCF Date: Friday, November 20, 2026 Kickoff: 5:00 p.m. CT / 6:00 p.m. ET Location: Acrisure Bounce House, Orlando, Florida Streaming: FOX Sports app with an eligible TV subscription Iowa State vs. UCF Injuries and Expected Starters Iowa State is expected to start Jaylen Raynor at quarterback, while running back Aiden Flora enters Friday's matchup following one of the best performances of his season. Flora rushed for 216 yards and three touchdowns against Cincinnati, bringing his season total to more than 1,100 rushing yards. For UCF, the quarterback situation is worth monitoring. Keyone Jenkins has dealt with an ankle injury, while Alonza Barnett III has also seen action at quarterback. Jenkins was listed as a game-time decision ahead of the Arizona State game, making his availability an important storyline heading into Friday. UCF running back Duke Watson was listed as unavailable against Arizona State, while Iowa State quarterback Connor Moberly was also listed as out against Cincinnati. The official Big 12 availability report for this matchup has not yet been released. This section will be updated as additional injury information becomes available. Iowa State vs. UCF Biggest Question: Who Stops the Run? Both teams would like to try and establish the run. Iowa State is led by star running back Aiden Flora, while UCF has a more balanced approach to the running attack, led by Duke Watson. Iowa State's offense has been far superior this season, ranking No. 28 in the country in yards per play, while UCF's offense is outside of the Top 100. However, it's UCF's defense that ranks in the Top 60 in yards per play, while Iowa State is outside the Top 100. Whoever wins this battle will have the leg up in this game on Friday night. Iowa State vs. UCF Prediction and Pick Prediction: Iowa State 27, UCF 23 Pick against the spread: Iowa State +1.5 Both teams have been better at home vs. the on the road, which is the only reason I am hesitant on this game for the Cyclones. I also don't want to overreact to their huge performance vs. Cincinnati last week. A road game on a Friday night is a much toughest spot. That being the case, UCF just hasn't earned my money in this spot, or the right to be a favorite. And it feels like the offense has either taken a step back, or just gotten confused since it had to move to back to Alonza Barnett at QB compared to where it was with Keyone Jenkins. UCF is last in the Big 12 in first downs and 15th in third-down conversions. And while Iowa State's defense hasn't been great, they've also played some of the most explosive offenses in the Big 12, like Utah, Arizona and Oklahoma State. I think that side of the ball can exceed expectations against a UCF offense that has been far from consistent. Iowa State vs. UCF FAQ What time is Iowa State vs. UCF? UCF is favored by 1.5 points in the November 15 betting market. Where is Iowa State vs. UCF being played? The game will take place at Acrisure Bounce House in Orlando, Florida. picks.blurb: Iowa State-UCF Prediction: Can The Cyclones Battle Through The Rain? IowaStateRoundtable 17 Members • 191 Posts IowaStateRoundtable IowaStateRoundtable Related stories Trending stories IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Iowa State-UCF Prediction: Can The Cyclones Battle Through The Rain? Brad Schultz Partner Nov 19, 2026 3:17 AM Published Nov 19, 2026 3:17 AM This matchup between 5-5 teams should be an all-out fight for bowl eligibility. Here's how Publisher Brad Schultz sees this one playing out. More Videos No one expected Iowa State football to be in the position it's in right now, and why would they? Jimmy Rogers had to rebuild this Cyclone program from the ground up after Matt Campbell left for Penn State and gutted the roster in the process. Some programs can endure such a teardown and instantly be in the national spotlight the following season, but few thought it could be done at Iowa State, one of the losingest Power Four college football programs. While it's certainly not all cupcakes and rainbows in Ames right now, the Cyclones currently sit at 5-5 – one win away from an improbable trip to a bowl game. But there's no time for Iowa State to celebrate just yet. It has two games to finish the job and get at least one win to secure bowl eligibility and continue its sudden momentum. The first game on the docket takes place on Friday against UCF. The Knights are also 5-5, so this matchup has the potential to be an all-out war in what looks to be soggy Florida weather in Orlando. Related stories More content will be coming out on Thursday, but in the meantime, here's how I see this matchup playing out. Matchup: Iowa State Cyclones (5-5, 3-4) @ UCF Knights (5-5, 3-4) Location: Acrisure Bounce House in Orlando, Florida Scheduled game time: Nov. 20 at 5 p.m. CDT Weather: 72 degrees with rain (flash flood warning have been issued) Announcers: Noah Reed (play-by-play) and Petros Papadakis (analyst) Radio: Cyclone Radio Network (John Walters, Eric Heft) Betting information (as of Nov. 18 and per DraftKings): UCF -2.5 | O/U: 48.5 As I've been saying all week, I feel like this is an extremely winnable game for Iowa State. While UCF does boast a really good win over BYU, the Knights have been extremely inconsistent under Scott Frost (who folks in the state of Iowa should know by now). They've alternated wins and losses since the dramatic win over the Cougars on Oct. 24 – a 41-9 drubbing at the hands of Baylor one week after the BYU victory, a last-second touchdown to beat Kansas, and a 13-point home loss to an Arizona State team that had to fly to Orlando the day of the game. Long story short, what UCF team are we going to see on Friday? We really don't know, and that's why I trust Iowa State in this spot. There's probably going to be a nice dose of cardinal and gold inside the Bounce House for this game, but that's not the only reason why I'm picking the Cyclones. The other reason why this game favors Iowa State is the weather. It's going to be a rainy slugfest in Orlando, but the Cyclones have the pleasure of having Aiden Flora on their team. He's doing incredible things every week and should get plenty of carries with a likely run-first game plan here. Neither defense is very good, but Flora is going to be the difference yet again. The Cyclones clinch bowl eligibility in the Sunshine State. Prediction: Iowa State 31, UCF 23

Let's take a look at this game from a betting perspective. Iowa State Cyclones vs. UCF Knights Prediction In my view, this matchup favors the UCF Knights. Why? UCF enters the game with a 4-2 home record. The Knights have defeated Kansas, BYU, and TCU this season. Meanwhile, Iowa State is 5-1 at home but 0-4 on the road, which is difficult to ignore when evaluating a game expected to be rather competitive. The Cyclones have been the better offensive team statistically, averaging 29.6 points per game compared to 23.4 points per game for UCF. away.headline: Iowa State women's coach Bill Fennelly suspended for a game for `inappropriate contact' with player
away.source: The Associated Press- Sports on MSN
away.blurb: Fennelly will sit out at Northern Iowa on Wednesday night. Associate head coach Caroline McCombs will direct the team that night. AMES, Iowa (AP) — Iowa State suspended women’s basketball coach Bill Fennelly one game Sunday night for “inappropriate contact” with a Cyclones player. Fennelly nudged the player’s head with his hand earlier Sunday in a 69-64 home victory over Illinois Chicago. The 69-year-old Bill Fennelly said last month he plans to retire at the end of the season, his 32nd as head coach at the school. “We cannot tolerate inappropriate contact between a coach or staff member and a student-athlete in practice or in competition, whether intentional or not,” athletic director Jared Benko said in a statement. “We have high expectations of all of our coaches, staff and student-athletes and we will not shy away from holding accountable those who fail to meet those expectations. I have met with Coach Fennelly and he has apologized to the student-athlete involved and regrets his actions.” “I want to apologize to the student-athlete and her family, her teammates and all of Cyclone Nation for allowing my emotions to get the best of me during our game,” Fennelly said in a statement. “I fully recognize that there are no situations where it is appropriate to make contact with a student-athlete in that way. I accept responsibility and will serve the suspension and I will do better moving forward.” The Cyclones are 5-0 this season. Fennelly is 661-335 with 24 NCAA Tournament appearances and 26 postseason appearances at Iowa State. On the Carriker Chronicles, Adam Carriker breaks down why Nebraska has a chance, what worries him most, and why he thinks this game could still be up for grabs in the fourth quarter. Nebraska’s shutout of Rutgers showed how good this defense can be. The running game also put together a complete performance, which gives the Huskers something to build on. But can they run the ball against Ohio State when the Buckeyes know it’s coming? Carriker wants Nebraska to run with a purpose and give Anthony Colandrea some quick answers in the passing game. Get the tight ends involved. Take a few shots downfield when the matchup is there. And when it’s third down, give Ohio State something it hasn’t already seen. At some point, somebody has to win a one-on-one matchup. The biggest question on defense is Jeremiah Smith. How does Rob Aurich keep a receiver that good from taking over the game? That job gets tougher with Andrew Marshall out. Carriker talks through how Nebraska can mix up its pressure and make Ohio State work for its yards. A couple of big plays can undo an otherwise good afternoon for the defense. The Huskers need to keep Smith from getting loose and give themselves a chance to get off the field on third down. Nebraska just shut out a Big Ten opponent on the road. The Huskers dispatched Rutgers 31–0 on Saturday, and while the Scarlet Knights aren't exactly setting the college football world on fire, shutting out a conference opponent is no small accomplishment. Now comes Ohio State. But these aren't the same Buckeyes we've grown accustomed to seeing. Ohio State has three losses. Three! In Columbus, that's practically grounds for declaring a state of emergency. And according to Ramsey from Eleven Warriors, who joined Monday Night Therapy this week, the problems aren't imaginary. The offensive line has struggled. The tight ends apparently believe blocking is an optional extracurricular activity. Special teams have been an adventure, and not the enjoyable kind. The Buckeyes are also starting true freshman quarterback Luke Fahey, who's talented but still learning on the job. Those are a lot of vulnerabilities for a program accustomed to simply reloading every season. Of course, Ohio State still has Jeremiah Smith. Nebraska can scheme, disguise coverages, and pressure the quarterback all afternoon, but Smith is capable of making one play that changes everything. So how does Nebraska keep him from doing that? Run. The. Damn. Ball. Control possession. Move the chains. Keep the clock running. Make Ohio State's offense spend as much time watching from the sideline as possible. And when it's third-and-two, perhaps we could actually gain two yards instead of getting unnecessarily creative. Just a thought. Nebraska's defense has momentum after its performance against Rutgers, and a home crowd in Lincoln should make life uncomfortable for a freshman quarterback. The opportunity is there. But opportunity and execution haven't always been particularly close friends in Lincoln. Nebraska vs. Ohio State Betting Odds The betting discussion has centered on Ohio State as a narrow favorite. Personally, I think Ohio State would deserve to be favored by six or seven points on a neutral field. But Memorial Stadium isn't neutral, and this isn't an Ohio State team without weaknesses. The Buckeyes have the talent to win this game. Nebraska has the opportunity to make that talent irrelevant for long stretches. Whether the Huskers can actually pull that off is another question entirely. Choose wisely. Play responsibly. And Go Big Red. Always.

The Wildcats got creative and stayed in the game until late, but this is still a shaky team that was happy to get close to five yards per carry. This is where that third down thing matters for the Huskers. Even after sputtering last week, Nebraska is still No. 1 in the Big Ten in third down conversions, and it's No. 1 in the nation in third down stops. Ohio State has a problem closing out drives with points, but it's able to get the chains moving. If the Buckeyes start stalling – which they likely will against this Husker defense that knows how to get off the field – this will be a struggle. Ohio State vs Nebraska Prediction, Betting Lines The talent isn't there for Nebraska compared to Ohio State, but this Buckeye team just isn't meshing like it should. It's still a very, very good team, but the production isn't there at the level it should be. Nebraska is overdue to be on the right side of a tight battle, and it's all about the turnovers. The Huskers are 5-1 when they force a takeaway, and 1-3 when they don't – the one win was over North Dakota from the FCS. Ohio State has turned the ball over nine times in the last five games. But it's hard to believe a program still among the winningest in history hasn't beaten a ranked opponent since a 35-32 win over Oregon on Sept. 17, 2016. Only Rutgers, at 46 in a row, has a longer losing streak against the Top 25. The Huskers' skid has covered the coaching runs of Mike Riley, Scott Frost, interim coach Mickey Joseph and now Matt Rhule, whose personal losing streak against the Top 25 stands at 21 over a combined seven seasons at Baylor and Nebraska. Nebraska nearly broke through against then-No. 7 Indiana on Oct. 10. The Huskers entered the fourth quarter leading by 11 points and lost 20-17. The next opportunity comes Saturday when No. 16 Ohio State visits. If the Huskers lose, they will presumably get another chance the day after Thanksgiving at Iowa, which is No. 13 this week. picks.headline: 'He's Really Turned the Corner': Nebraska Interim OC Glenn Thomas Praises Jamal Rule, Previews Ohio State
picks.blurb: 'He's Really Turned the Corner': Nebraska Interim OC Glenn Thomas Praises Jamal Rule, Previews Ohio State - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games Giannis red hot vs. Bucks Boone's trade charts Cowboys DC latest Jamal Rule has totaled 748 all-purpose yards and six touchdowns through the first 10 games of his collegiate career. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Trevor Tarr · Nebraska Cornhuskers On SI Tue, November 17, 2026 at 8:35 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Saturday against Rutgers, the Huskers ran the damn ball . In Week 12, against Ohio State, they may look to do the same. The task won't be easy, though, as NU is set to face the 12th-best run defense in college football. As interim offensive coordinator Glenn Thomas previewed Nebraska's Senior Day matchup with the Buckeyes, freshman running back Jamal Rule was among the players who earned his praise. Here's what Thomas had to say Tuesday about the Huskers' offensive approach heading into their final home game of 2026. Jamal Rule leads Nebraska with 635 rushing yards on 110 attempts. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Rule quickly adjusted to the college game, totaling 411 all-purpose yards and all six of his touchdowns through the first three games of his freshman campaign. An ankle injury in the first quarter against Michigan State then limited his production and impact until last week. The freshman bounced back in a big way against Rutgers , carrying the ball 22 times for 103 yards. When Thomas was asked about Rule's performance and recovery from the injury, he was was quick to praise his progress. "He's been great," Thomas said. "He's really turned the corner and is running hard. What excites you as much as anything is his physicality, but also his ability to make some yards after contact. First play of the game, safety comes up and, you know, makes some contact, and he was able to get six or eight yards after that." "Those are the things that we continue to try and promote and be aware of," Thomas continued. "Cause, you know, if you block a four-yard run, you want to get six or eight; you don't want to get a four-yard run. So, he brings that element to us, and I think that really creates an advantage for us as far as staying in front of the chains." Gibson Pyle has played a combined 146 snaps over the last two weeks and has been charged with just one quarterback hurry during that time. | Nebraska Athletics NU's success on the ground was also aided by several offensive linemen who weren't in the starting lineup when the season began. While Thomas praised the entire unit, he singled out Gunnar Gottula and Gibson Pyle, who combined for 109 offensive snaps against Rutgers and allowed just one pressure between them in Saturday's win. "Man, that's been a nice advantage," he said. "We really have a lot of flexibility on the offensive line with Gunnar. Gibby got in there and played a bunch; you know, in the last couple of games, he's played quite a bit. So, there's a lot of confidence in those guys when they come in, and I don't feel like we've missed a beat with those guys." The Huskers ran for 237 yards and two touchdowns on 43 rushing attempts against the Scarlet Knights. While Rutgers' defense ranked last in the Big Ten against the run, Nebraska's offensive line and running backs still deserve credit. The challenge now is finding a way to replicate that success against a defense with much better talent all around. Ohio State safety Simeon Caldwell celebrates a pass breakup against Northwestern. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect That is sure to be difficult against Ohio State. Thomas suggested Nebraska could use heavier offensive formations, similar to what the Huskers did against Rutgers, while emphasizing the importance of having multiple schematic answers ready when the Buckeyes adjust. "They're going to have their ways to attack us," he said. "So, we have to have, whether it's schematic plans, formations, you know, a variety of things that we can hopefully do on our end to take advantage of what they're doing schematically. That's the game within the game, as far as trying to put those guys in a position; the best possible way to have success." Carter Nelson has caught four passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns in Nebraska's last three games. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Nebraska's play-action passing game also found success against Rutgers, as in-state products Carter Nelson and Luke Lindenmeyer each hauled in a touchdown. While Lindenmeyer has been a reliable contributor for several years, Nelson has emerged as a welcome addition in recent weeks. "I think he's a new player," Thomas said regarding the former No. 3 tight end in the 2024 recruiting class. "I'm super excited for where he's at, not only off the field, but on the field. He's really taken the next step since the injury. He's playing fast; he's playing confident; he's physical. "He's still a work in progress as far as having, you know, all the offseason, lack of reps. So, he's continued to grow within the season, and it's been exciting to see, and that has translated to the field." While Thomas noted that Nelson needs to work on his throwing motion following his failed pass attempt on a fake punt against Rutgers, it's clear the Huskers plan to utilize him more as a receiving threat. Players like Nelson, Rule, and Pyle are continuing to develop before our eyes, and Nebraska will need each of them to step up against Ohio State. Kickoff for Saturday's contest is set for 11 a.m. Central, with the Huskers entering the matchup as slight underdogs. How well those players handle their expanded roles could go a long way toward determining NU's chances of pulling off the upset. We'll find out how they fare soon enough. home.headline: Andrew Marshall injury could keep Nebraska from taking the next step in evolution
home.blurb: Marshall missed the Huskers’ game against Rutgers this past weekend, and on Monday, head coach Matt Rhule confirmed that the star defensive back is out for the rest of the season. When Nebraska faces off against Ohio State on Saturday, the Huskers know they won’t have to face quarterback Julian Sayin . However, they’ll still have to face all-time great wide receiver Jeremiah Smith, which is why losing Andrew Marshall is a big blow. Rhule said that Marshall suffered a stress fracture in his leg against Illinois but continued to play after suffering the injury. Since that game, Marshall has undergone surgery to repair the fracture and has played his last down for Nebraska in his college football career. Marshall finished the 2026 season with 28 tackles, an interception, and a team-high six pass breakups. He’s long been considered one of the best defensive backs in the country, and Rhule made that point when addressing the injury. Andrew Marshall season-ending injury leaves Nebraska football without shutdown corner vs. Ohio State “I think he’s as good as there is in the country and I think everyone knows it,” Rhule said during his Monday press conference. “I think everyone’s seen it.” The California native is one of NU’s best transfer-portal stories after arriving from Idaho before the 2025 campaign. Nebraska routinely lined him up opposite an opponent’s best receiver and often left him in one-on-one coverage while devoting defensive help elsewhere. Marshall was targeted just 44 times this season and allowed just 15 receptions for 237 yards. 93 of those yards came against Illinois, as it was easily his worst game of the season. Playing on a bum leg certainly explains why he struggled against Illinois’ Colin Dixon, who was recently named to the latest Fred Biletnikoff Award watch list. Nebraska started Victor Evans and freshman Danny Odem at cornerback against Rutgers and will move forward with the same duo along with Jeremiah Charles. Junior Larry Tarver is also set to see more rotational action. Without Nebraska’s shutdown corner, beating Ohio State became even tougher on Monday. It’s unlikely that one corner will be assigned to Smith the way defensive coordinator Rob Aurich might have assigned Marshall if he were healthy. Nebraska is obviously hoping that a change in offensive coordinator and the end of the four-game losing streak will allow the Huskers to finish the season strong. Beating Ohio State in Lincoln is never easy, but this version of the Buckeyes has shown they are flawed. The latest odds for Wisconsin vs. Purdue paint a sad reality for Luke Fickell
picks.blurb: The latest odds for Wisconsin vs. Purdue paint a sad reality for Luke Fickell Skip to main content About Us Wisconsin Badgers News Wisconsin Football Wisconsin Basketball FanSided NCAA Sites Wisconsin Badgers In The Pros Wisconsin Football Recruiting Wisconsin Football All-Time Lists Wisconsin Basketball Recruiting Wisconsin Women's Basketball Wisconsin Basketball All-Time Lists The Wisconsin Badgers were terrible against the Maryland Terrapins on Saturday. There's no other way to slice it or dice it, it was disgraceful at best and a 'fire everybody in the whole football department' at worst. Which is what many of the Wisconsin fans are calling for. Maryland had only one Big Ten game all season and had fired their head coach. The Terrapins are a basement-dwelling Big Ten team. So, what does Vegas do for Wisconsin when the Badgers take on another basement-dwelling team, Purdue? Well, they give them barely favorable odds. Can't trust them. The best thing Wisconsin has going for itself in this Purdue game is that it's the Boilermakers that the Terrapins beat a couple of games ago. The Badgers enter their final road game of the season against a *checks notes* 3-7 Purdue team as barely a favorite. At 5.5 points, Vegas assumes that Wisconsin can only beat the Boilermakers with two field goals... or worse. That's alarming and paints a bleak reality for Luke Fickell. In his banner year, the "prove-it" year, the one when everything lined up perfectly. He had the bigger budget, the supposedly better coaching staff, a deeper quarterback room, a way more favorable schedule, and yet, with only two games to go, Wisconsin is barely considered a favorite over Purdue. It's hard to express how disappointing that is, when Wisconsin should be looking at this game as a "rest the starters" in the 4th-quarter situation; they are staring down the barrel of another potential upset. If there's anything that shows Wisconsin should move on from Luke Fickell and/or some of his staff, it's this bleak reminder that the program is actually in the same place as last year, but with an easier schedule. ESPN has the probabilities a bit higher than Vegas at 65% according to their analytics, but still, that's not great. And if Wisconsin can't find a way to beat Purdue, and beat them without any drama, there's no reason Luke Fickell needs to get on the flight back to Madison. And yet the big fear is that this 6-win season will be sold to Wisconsin fans as a step forward and that the Badgers should continue to let him run it back. The $21 million buy-out may force Shawn Eichorst to gaslight the fanbase, as Chris McIntosh did. Hopefully, I'm wrong, but it feels like we are headed that direction. This Purdue game needs to be a blowout; winning by 5 or 6 points won't be good enough. Fans should be embarrassed that Vegas even suggests so. away.blurb: Wisconsin (6-4, 4-3) suffered a frustrating 24-21 loss Saturday at Maryland (4-6, 2-5), a result that only intensified questions surrounding the program's direction . Having already handed out grades for the offense , Badgers On SI now breaks down the defense and special teams. Donovan Dunmore was thrust into an expanded role at cornerback despite limited previous experience and showed promise as a tackler, finishing with seven tackles (four solo) and a tackle for loss. His coverage was less encouraging, as the freshman allowed receptions on all three targets for 36 yards and earned a 49.8 PFF coverage grade. The safety rotation was also disrupted when Matt Jung suffered an apparent leg injury while recovering a fumble near Wisconsin's goal line late in the second quarter. Matthew Traynor subsequently saw his first meaningful action, logging 30 snaps and finishing with six tackles (four solo) and a respectable 66.3 PFF overall grade. However, his fourth-quarter personal foul for a late hit out of bounds was a moment to forget. Darrion Dupree provided respectable production in the return game, totaling 56 yards on two kickoff returns, though neither produced a game-changing play. Overall, it was a fairly steady showing from Wisconsin's special teams outside of West's second-quarter miscue. Wisconsin Football Report Card: Injuries Take Their Toll on Badgers Defense Skip to main content SI.COM The absence of star edge rusher Sebastian Cheeks presented a challenge for Wisconsin's defensive front, and his presence was sorely missed. Tyreese Fearbry generated two pressures but failed to provide the necessary spark, earning a dismal 18.4 PFF tackling grade. Nick Clayton saw his workload increase to a career-high 45 snaps and made little impact as a pass rusher, though he fared well against the run and finished with five tackles (four solo). Nolan Vils was a bright spot along the interior, recording four tackles (two solo) and half a tackle for loss while earning a team-best 80.7 PFF overall grade. Defensive tackles Charles Perkins and Hammond Russell IV each generated a pressure, but Perkins struggled as a tackler, missing two tackles and receiving a 25.5 grade in that department. Collectively, Wisconsin held Maryland to 107 rushing yards on 39 attempts (2.7 YPC), another strong showing from a run defense that has been a consistent strength. However, the inability to generate meaningful pressure proved costly as backup quarterback Cardell Williams settled into a rhythm, completing 21-of-23 passes for 183 yards and a touchdown. The Badgers desperately need Cheeks back to bolster a pass rush that struggled to disrupt the Terrapins’ aerial attack. The Tar Heels announced Tuesday that Avdalas underwent surgery to repair the injury. The sophomore suffered the injury during Friday night’s 78-70 loss to Georgia at the Dean E. Smith Center. Avdalas is expected to miss a significant portion of North Carolina’s nonconference schedule, along with the beginning of ACC play, as he begins his recovery. The injury is a tough blow for first-year head coach Michael Malone, who has relied on Avdalas as an important part of the Tar Heels’ backcourt rotation. Through North Carolina’s first four games, Avdalas averaged 9.0 points, 3.5 rebounds and a team-leading 3.8 assists per game. He also recorded 15 assists, the most on the team, while ranking fourth in scoring. Avdalas started all four games for the Tar Heels after transferring from Virginia Tech during the offseason. During his freshman season with the Hokies, the 6-foot-9 guard averaged 12.1 points and 4.6 assists per game. He started all 31 games and earned ACC Rookie of the Week honors twice. His size, versatility and playmaking ability made him an important addition to Malone’s first North Carolina roster. Tar Heels Must Adjust Without Neo Avdalas With Avdalas sidelined, North Carolina will need other players to take on additional responsibilities in the backcourt. Terrence Brown, Isaiah Denis, Angelo Brizzi and Jaydon Young could all see increased opportunities as the Tar Heels look to replace Avdalas’ production and playmaking. Brown has been one of North Carolina’s leading offensive contributors early in the season, while Denis has also provided valuable minutes in the backcourt. North Carolina enters the next stretch of its schedule at 3-1 following the loss to Georgia. The Tar Heels will look to get back on track when they host Marshall on Friday, Nov. 20. home.headline: Billy Edwards Jr.'s status remains uncertain as UNC's initial injury report for Virginia is revealed
home.blurb: The ACC released the initial injury reports for this weekend's contests, and, unsurprisingly, starting quarterback Billy Edwards Jr. is listed as questionable. While we all expected Edwards Jr. to be listed as questionable, given his status for Saturday is still very much in question, we did find out that two defensive standouts already have been ruled out. Melkart Abou Jaoude, who has dealt with injuries all season long, has already been ruled out for UNC's second-to-last regular-season game. Greg Smith III , who was suspended for the first half of the game after being involved in a postgame brawl last weekend, has also been ruled out. Virginia has an extensive list of players already ruled out for Saturday afternoon's clash against UNC. In total, 13 players have already been ruled out, as the injury bug could force more to be sidelined before kickoff occurs in just a few days. The story to follow for UNC will be Edwards Jr.'s status. Because he was limited in practice, there's some doubt he'll be able to play against the Cavaliers, but it all depends on how the rest of the week shapes up. If he's unable to go, expect true freshman Travis Burgess, who came in relief following Edwards Jr.'s injury against Louisville, to make his first collegiate start. If you thought that Bill Belichick was going to tip his hand midweek as to who will be his starting quarterback on Saturday afternoon at Virginia, well, the joke's on you. UNC to be without two defensive stars on Saturday vs. Virginia At this point, there's no clarification as to whether Smith is hurt or if UNC is making his suspension a full game to penalize him for his actions. Based on what we know about Belichick, he likely will wait as long as he can to reveal what the Tar Heels' plan at quarterback is. For now, we all remain on Billy Edwards Jr. watch, waiting to see if the veteran will be able to suit up and play. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings Brad Crawford and Chris Hummer reveal their picks for college football's biggest matchups of the weekend Getty Images Call college football's Week 12 schedule a breather if you want to -- just keep that same energy again Saturday night when there are a handful of results we never saw coming. There isn't a single AP Top 25 matchup on the schedule, but 10 ranked teams are single-digit favorites on the road. How many of them are you willing to trust with their College Football Playoff seeding and potential conference title hopes on the line? This is the kind of slate that looks harmless until a favorite trails by a couple of touchdowns early or starts feeling the heat in the second half of a game that could go in either direction. We're picking the biggest games of Week 12, including a few where the road favorite might spend Sunday figuring out how much damage one afternoon did to its résumé. Season results : Brad Crawford (67-34 straight up, 45-55-1 ATS); Chris Hummer (73-28 straight up, 50–50-1 ATS) We're in a futile state of affairs, folks. I'm afraid the hole is too deep for me to crawl out of this season to continue my winning streak against Hummer in our annual head-to-head picks battle. We both had losing records last week, but he still picked up a game on me and now holds a five-game lead with a couple of weekends left. No. 14 Ohio State (-3.5) at Nebraska Hummer ( Ohio State -3.5): These are two good and flawed teams. Both are top 20 defenses. Both have largely struggled on offense since mid-October. An injury to Julian Sayin caused Ohio State's issues. Tougher competition caught up to the Huskers. I just don't see Nebraska moving the ball all that well against the Buckeyes. Luke Fahey has played pretty well the last two weeks. He and the Buckeyes' offense do enough. … Ohio State 27, Nebraska 21. Crawford (Ohio State -3.5): Y'all know Matt Rhule's record against top-25 opponents, right? I can keep things short here if so. The Buckeyes still have an outside shot at getting in the CFP discussion as a bubble team with convincing wins this week and next (against Michigan ). Jeremiah Smith needs a monster outing on the road to remain in the frontrunner discussion for the Heisman. He has scored in seven straight games but is no longer the first player voters think of when top players are mentioned. ... Ohio State 27, Nebraska 20. No. 10 BYU (-6.5) at Kansas Hummer ( BYU -6.5): Kansas is an odd team. The Jayhawks are top 45 nationally in both yards per play and yards allowed per play. But they're also just 2-5 in the Big 12 and have struggled with both turnovers and injuries. The problem for Kansas is that it can struggle to stop the run, and that's what BYU does best. I could see this being close. But I'll take the team with a lot on the line that's been incredibly consistent this season. … BYU 31, Kansas 24. Crawford (BYU -6.5): At 4-6 overall this season, the Jayhawks need consecutive wins over BYU and Oklahoma State to reach bowl eligibility. It's not going to come to fruition, unfortunately. BYU has to win and look good doing it to avoid dropping in the CFP rankings, and there's no margin for error in the conference title discussion behind Utah and Texas Tech . BYU does not control its own destiny, but if the Cougars win out, they're going to have a strong argument for inclusion. ... BYU 34, Kansas 20. No. 15 Iowa (-6.5) at Illinois Hummer ( Iowa -6.5): The Illini are a better team than some of the advanced stats would suggest, largely because their defense did a 180 after a coordinator change. But the Hawkeyes are the better overall team, especially if they get decent quarterback play from Hank Brown . Iowa should control the lines of scrimmage and the general pace of the game. The only thing that could flip that is turnovers, which is something that Iowa's struggled with in losses this season. But the Hawkeyes get it done. … Iowa 27, Illinois 20. Crawford (Iowa -6.5): Can Katin Houser put the Fighting Illini in position to win this one against a defense that rarely gives up big plays? He's coming off a three-interception game against UCLA , but has been solid for the most part throughout the campaign with 18 touchdowns and eight interceptions. Iowa's playing with stakes in this one, with a chance to finish 10-2 overall by winning out. The Hawkeyes are one of six bubble teams, I'm projecting, that are battling for two at-large spots over the rest of the campaign. That matters here. ... Iowa 24, Illinois 17. LSU (-1.5) at No. 9 Tennessee Hummer ( LSU -1.5): It's wild to see LSU favored on the road at Tennessee given their records and season. But I agree with Vegas. I think, at least on paper, LSU is the better team. It just comes down to whether Sam Leavitt can avoid turnovers. I think after a disaster against Texas , he plays clean. Tennessee's O-line is going to struggle to dominate in the run game against LSU's defensive front. The Tigers get their first win over a ranked opponent of the Lane Kiffin era. ... LSU 24, Tennessee 20. Crawford (Tennessee +1.5): I said last week that I would never pick Lane Kiffin to win (or cover) against a ranked team again if the Tigers burned me against Texas and it happened -- so I'm sticking with my promise. The Vols are a couple wins away from wrapping up a first-round home game, potentially more if they can find a way into the SEC Championship Game. If I'm Josh Heupel, I'd rather have an extra week of playoff prep time and let Georgia , Alabama or Texas duke it out in Atlanta ahead of the postseason. Jim Knowles finds a way to turn Sam Leavitt over and the Vols prevail. ... Tennessee 23, LSU 20. No. 12 Texas Tech (-3.5) at Baylor Hummer ( Baylor +3.5): The Red Raiders have found something since switching to Thomas Castellanos at quarterback. They've averaged 47 points per game over the last three weeks, emerging as a dynamic run-heavy offense. Baylor matches up reasonably well defensively in this one. The Bears are a top-20 run defense and have largely contained mobile QBs this year. This game will come down to how DJ Lagway fares against a Texas Tech pass defense that's struggled this year. I think this game is close. But the Red Raiders win it late. … Texas Tech 31, Baylor 28. Crawford (Texas Tech -3.5): I took Baylor and the points last week against BYU and immediately regretted it early when the Cougars began bludgeoning the Bears at the line of scrimmage and limiting DJ Lagway's production in the passing game. Will playing at home against the Big 12's second-best team through 11 weeks alter the mentality here? Tommy Castellanos has been great for the Red Raiders over his last three starts, and I don't see that changing. ... Texas Tech 38, Baylor 31. No. 8 Indiana (-8.5) at Washington Hummer ( Washington +8.5): This screams a trap game in Seattle. But Washington just hasn't been the program everyone expected this year. The offense continues to struggle -- the Huskies rank 125th nationally in yards per carry -- and that's not going to look any better against an elite Indiana defense. How Washington fares will depend on whether its defense, which has been solid this year, holds up against an Indiana offense that still seems stuck in the mud. This is the type of game Indiana wins ugly. … Indiana 24, Washington 17. Crawford (Indiana -8.5): Curt Cignetti needs to be careful. Politicking for his team to the CFP committee to potentially better the Hoosiers' seeding is one thing, but this isn't the same Indiana squad that was demolishing the opposition last season. They're winning with defense and just enough execution offensively to get by. He has tried to flex a schedule this season that, let's be honest, has been more than favorable for the Hoosiers. Here's another opportunity this weekend to beat a good opponent, but not a great one. ... Indiana 27, Washington 17. No. 4 UCLA (-5.5) at Michigan Hummer (Michigan +5.5): I feel like I've picked against UCLA every week this season and they keep winning games. So why stop now? These are two teams beating each other with a club. They have two elite defenses and two offenses that can struggle at times. The difference is UCLA is pretty efficient (22nd nationally in yards per play) while Michigan is anything but (124th nationally in yards per play). Still, this is the type of game the Wolverines will stay in throughout because of their defense. The offense just needs to make enough plays to keep it close. … UCLA 17, Michigan 14. Crawford (UCLA -5.5): This is a spooky line to say the least. Every week, oddsmakers are waiting for the Bruins to catch a loss with these single-digit spreads, but it hasn't happened yet. I don't think it comes in Ann Arbor, either. If you're going to pick an outright loss for UCLA, wait until rivalry weekend aga

Now, in just its third year as a Big Ten school, UCLA can go to the Big Ten Championship game with one more win in its last two games. Michigan is looking for anything positive at this point. The season crashed through the floor, going 2-5 in Big Ten play – losing to Oregon and Michigan State by a combined score of 46-13 – and now it needs a win in the last two games just to go to a bowl game. UCLA vs Michigan: Quick Hits Michigan closes with a bang: losing to Oregon 31-7 last week in Eugene, hosting UCLA this week, and finishing with the showdown against Ohio State in Columbus. UCLA closes at USC next week. It won't need the win if it can beat the Wolverines, but obviously, it's the rivalry game the Bruins want. The two teams haven't played since 2000, a 23-20 UCLA win. Starting in 1956 with a 42-13 win, UCLA is 8-3 in the series. Michigan has turned it over multiple times in every game except for the wins over Oklahoma and Rutgers, and gave it away once in the loss to Iowa. It turned it over 13 times in the last six games. UCLA is No. 1 in the nation with 30 takeaways. Why Michigan Will Win UCLA isn't the type of team that wings the ball all over the yard. It's a tough, hard-nosed team, but it's not going to run away and hide with a big offensive explosion. The Bruins will play exactly the way Michigan wants. UCLA will need to run the ball, keep the tempo low, and rely on the lines – fine with the Wolverines. This is where the Wolverines can play it tough on the lines, work the field position battle, and try to keep this tight into the final few minutes. Despite the issues over the rough run, the defense is still among the ten best in America. UCLA vs Michigan Prediction, Betting Lines UCLA will have to work for it, but the defense will come up with the stop it needs late against the punchless Michigan offense. The Wolverines will come out fired up and cranked for the moment, marching down the field with a stunningly crisp opening scoring drive. But UCLA doesn't panic. The Bruin defense will be a rock on third downs, the offense will take the field goals and points when they're available, and Michigan's offense won't be able to take care of its opportunities to pull off the upset. Playing the role of spoiler this week are the Michigan Wolverines (5-5). Michigan has not lived up to expectations in their first year under Kyle Whittingham, as they’re currently scraping by to make a bowl game. With UCLA and Ohio State on the schedule, Michigan needs a massive upset win to reach bowl eligibility. Could it happen here? Not many people believe so, and the market pegs UCLA as a- 3.5-point road favorite with a game total of 37.5 points. In other words, don’t expect many points from either team. Will Michigan start Tommy Carr or Bryce Underwood this week? Whittingham said the two will battle it out after Carr replaced Underwood in the 31-7 loss to Oregon. UCLA outlasted Illinois, 22-14, on Friday night, but not without drama. The Bruins Ty Dieffenbach went down with an injury in the second quarter, then returned on the first drive of the fourth quarter following the Illini’s first score of the game (12-7). Like UCLA has done all season, they scored 10 points in the fourth quarter and had explosive plays left and right. UCLA built on their nation-leading 30 takeaways with three interceptions off Illinois and held the Illini to 240 total yards of offense. Let’s dive into the schools on both sides of the ball, look at a few key players, and see where the numbers take us. away.headline: 2 Michigan football starters ruled out for UCLA game
away.blurb: Michigan football has ruled out two key starters for the game against UCLA – and could be down more than that. Wide receiver JJ Buchanan is lost for the season while offensive tackle Blake Frazier, who coach Kyle Whittingham said earlier in the week was a long shot to play, has also been ruled out, according to the Big Ten's availability report released on Wednesday, Nov. 18. But beyond that, five other starters are listed as questionable: wide receiver Andrew Marsh, edge rusher John Henry Daley, offensive lineman Brady Norton, safety Rod Moore and tight end Jalen Hoffman. With Buchanan out, Marsh is unquestionably the No. 1 pass-catching option. Marsh has a team-high 48 grabs that have led to 459 yards and one touchdown this season. Last week, he was targeted on 14 of Michigan's 20 passes between quarterbacks Tommy Carr and Bryce Underwood. Moore tore his ACL in the spring of 2024 and missed all of that season. He tried to return in 2025 after more offseason complications with his knee, but suited up for just three games in the middle of the season before he was shut down the rest of the year. Channing Goodwin, Kendrick Bell and Jaylen Pile are all also listed as questionable. Ty Dieffenbach injury updates: UCLA QB returns after exiting in first half after hard hit - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Jordan Mendoza, USA TODAY · USA TODAY Sports Sat, November 14, 2026 at 3:53 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads PASADENA, CA — UCLA quarterback Ty Dieffenbach suffered an injury on a hard hit late in the first half against Illinois on Friday, Nov. 13. But it appears to not be an absolutely devastating hit for the Bruins . With 35 seconds left in the second quarter, Dieffenbach tried to throw the ball away when he got tripped up and was clearly in immediate pain. He was visibly shaken as he was attended to by support staff, and he appeared to indicate he had a left shoulder injury. After a few minutes he was helped up and taken to the sideline. Once the teams headed to the locker room, Dieffenbach went in appearing to not move his left arm and was limping. Ty Dieffenbach latest injury news Dieffenbach suffered an "upper body injury," according to the Fox broadcast. However, he emerged from the locker room with about four minutes left in the third quarter with a sleeve on his left arm, as the Rose Bowl crowd cheered. Dieffenbach was back on the field for UCLA late in the third quarter and played the remainder of the game. "I kind of went down a little awkward on the tackle, and my arm got caught up underneath, but it just got a little tight on me, and it's nothing serious," he said postgame. The Bruins got their quarterback to engineer another win. He reignited the offense, throwing a key fourth quarter touchdown to Semaj Morgan that strengthened the lead. UCLA held on to beat Illinois 22-14 to move to 10-0. Dieffenbach went 13-for-20 for 232 yards with two touchdowns and one interception, with 28 rushing yards. The injury was a big scare to UCLA's quarterback room as Dieffenbach has played in place of starter Nico Iamaleava after Iamaleava suffered a season ending injury against Oregon on Oct. 10. Dieffenbach has stepped up and kept the Bruins one of two undefeated teams left in the country, at 9-0 for the first time since 1998 with a shot at their first College Football Playoff appearance. Prior to the injury, Dieffenbach was 8-for-13 for 168 yards with one touchdown and one interception, leading UCLA to a 10-0 lead over Illinois. home.headline: Oregon vs. Michigan State injury report reveals more Ducks injuries and a major Spartans dilemma
home.blurb: Given that Oregon faces off against Michigan State on Friday Night , the initial injury report for this matchup came out a day sooner, with the schedule being pushed up a day. On Tuesday Night, the first injury report revealed the status of Jordon Davison, Douglas Utu, Jerry Mixon, Bear Alexander, and, surprisingly, Michigan State backup QB Cam Fancher. The best news for the Oregon Ducks was that offensive lineman Douglas Utu did not appear on the first injury report. The veteran guard missed time in the second half with what appeared to be a leg injury, but it appears that he'll return to the lineup this weekend. Defensive Tackle Bear Alexander appeared to have suffered an ankle injury vs. Michigan, but he returned to the game and is probable for Friday Night's matchup. Where the concerns start for Dan Lanning's group is with the status of linebacker Jerry Mixon, who missed the Michigan game. It was stated that Jerry Mixon tweaked something in warmups for the showdown with the Wolverines, but based on the fact that he's doubtful for this weekend's game, it appears to be more serious than a simple tweak. Even more disappointing is the status of Jordon Davison, who's been out since the first half of the Northwestern game. Dan Lanning shared that Davison was out of his walking boot, but he won't return to the field this weekend, putting all eyes on the showdown with the Huskies to end the season. Milivojevic remains out. Making matters more concerning for the Spartans is the fact that backup quarterback Cam Fancher is listed as questionable, as they could be forced to turn to their third-string QB against a stout Oregon defense. As the week goes on, the Spartans side of the report is going to be important to follow with 7 players listed as questionable, which can truly go either way. The good news for Oregon is that they're far from the only team dealing with serious injury issues, but it's also disappointing to see how many teams have been knocked down a level with all these injuries. The Oregon Ducks head into the final two games of the regular season looking to build on the momentum of this three-game winning streak, and to continue making a case for a College Football Playoff bid. Among the two teams standing in the Ducks' way are the Michigan State Spartans with a 3-7 record this season. While the Spartans have struggled, anything can happen in college football, and as Oregon continues to be plagued with injuries, the Ducks continue to dig deeper into the depth chart. This weekend, Dan Lanning and the Ducks will likely look across to the opposing sideline, and see that they're not alone dealing with rampant injuries. home.headline: 2 Michigan football starters ruled out for UCLA game
home.blurb: Michigan football has ruled out two key starters for the game against UCLA – and could be down more than that. Wide receiver JJ Buchanan is lost for the season while offensive tackle Blake Frazier, who coach Kyle Whittingham said earlier in the week was a long shot to play, has also been ruled out, according to the Big Ten's availability report released on Wednesday, Nov. 18. But beyond that, five other starters are listed as questionable: wide receiver Andrew Marsh, edge rusher John Henry Daley, offensive lineman Brady Norton, safety Rod Moore and tight end Jalen Hoffman. With Buchanan out, Marsh is unquestionably the No. 1 pass-catching option. Marsh has a team-high 48 grabs that have led to 459 yards and one touchdown this season. Last week, he was targeted on 14 of Michigan's 20 passes between quarterbacks Tommy Carr and Bryce Underwood. Moore tore his ACL in the spring of 2024 and missed all of that season. He tried to return in 2025 after more offseason complications with his knee, but suited up for just three games in the middle of the season before he was shut down the rest of the year. Channing Goodwin, Kendrick Bell and Jaylen Pile are all also listed as questionable. This article originally appeared on Detroit Free Press: 2 Michigan football starters ruled out for UCLA game Start the day smarter. Get all the news you need in your inbox each morning. Daley, who missed the Halloween contest at Rutgers, has been a mainstay on the report. He injured his Achilles last season and required surgery in the offseason, which he rehabbed from for more than seven months this offseason. THE WINDS OF CHANGE: Kyle Whittingham's seat getting hotter with new Michigan athletic director inbound Norton missed last week's 31-7 loss to Oregon with an undisclosed injury but if he could play it could be a boost to an offensive line that's been debilitated with injuries all season. Hoffman has been one of U-M's most utilized tight ends this season, averaging 37 snaps per game the past four weeks and is second in the room with nine receptions for 78 yards. As for Moore, this will be the final game at Michigan Stadium for the sixth-year senior, who has won a national championship with the program and been an All-Big Ten player, but dealt with injury trouble the past two seasons. He's only missed one game this season at Rutgers, but played just six snaps the week prior against Indiana after appearing to injure his ankle on an interception against Penn State. Moore has 33 tackles, one interception and one pass defended this year. Tony Garcia is the Michigan beat writer for the Detroit Free Press. Former Georgia QB Aaron Murray makes his prediction for LSU vs Tennessee Former Georgia quarterback Aaron Murray predicted last week that Tennessee would beat Texas A&M by 13 points last week (the Vols won by 15 points), but he's not making the same kind of prediction for the LSU game. Murray has the Tigers taking down the Vols on Saturday, predicting that LSU will leave Neyland Stadium with a 23-17 win. One of the main reasons Murray is predicting an LSU win is because the Vols will be without Mike Matthews. “This (LSU) defense is going to be able to put you in third-and-long situations,” said Murray. “And they're going to be able to get to the quarterback with Princewill Umanmielen and Jordan Ross coming off the edge. “… Can Tennessee's offense, without Matthews and with a banged up quarterback — it's possibly Faizon Brandon back in there playing quarterback — get the job done against LSU in this matchup? I don't feel very confident. Which is why I'm going with LSU 23-17 in this football game. If Mike Matthews was healthy, and if [George MacIntyre] — I don't know what the knee is right now, maybe he's 100 percent for the game [and I would feel different]. But still, no Mike Matthews. I think that's a big problem for the Tennessee Volunteers. So I think LSU wins the game.” I think that's a fair prediction from Murray. There are certainly questions about the Vols' offense without Matthews. The junior wide receiver was easily Tennessee's most dynamic playmaker. But LSU has failed to finish games in the fourth quarter this season and that's an area where Tennessee has thrived. If the Vols can get this game to the fourth quarter, I like their chances. But if they get to the fourth quarter and they're down multiple scores, it could be too big of a hill for Tennessee's offense to climb. ‘I know in that room' – The biggest reason the CFP committee is giving for ranking Alabama so high will make Tennessee fans even more mad The Tennessee Volunteers dropped one spot in the College Football Playoff rankings this week despite their road win over the Texas A&M Aggies. ‘Months of rehab' – Vols insider gives the latest on WR Mike Matthews and whether he could be back at Tennessee in 2027 Tennessee Volunteers wide receiver Mike Matthews will miss the rest of the 2026 season after suffering a season-ending knee injury against the Texas A&M Aggies this past weekend. away.blurb: Star junior tight end Trey'Dez Green is no longer listed on the report released Wednesday, Oct. 21, signaling his possible return to the field for No. 17 LSU (5-2, 2-2 SEC). His removal from the injury report means Green (6-7, 240) will be available to play against Auburn (4-2, 2-2) inside Jordan-Hare Stadium Saturday (11 a.m. CT, ABC). Initially, his injury was feared to be worse than what it ended up being. But his possible return to action after just four weeks is quicker than it was projected. Two weeks ago, Kiffin said that Green was "getting closer" to returning. "If there's anybody that's going to come back sooner than maybe what people think, it would be him," Kiffin said. "He is out of the brace and moving it. So, getting closer." Freshman defensive lineman Richard Anderson is the new name to the injury report for LSU, and he is listed as doubtful. LSU has had rough injury luck this season with major key players getting hurt. Senior linebacker Whit Weeks fractured his fibula during the Texas A&M three weeks ago and his return to the field is uncertain. Junior safety Dashawn Spears suffered a season-ending knee injury in the Ole Miss game. Green sprained his knee in the game against Ole Miss a month ago and has missed the last four games for Lane Kiffin and LSU. As it stands, LSU will be without four players for sure against Auburn in Weeks, Spears, wide receiver Phillip Wright III and linebacker Charles Ross II. home.headline: Will Tennessee beat LSU in Lane Kiffin's return to Neyland Stadium? Our pick
home.blurb: Can Tennessee pass the ball effectively with Mike Matthews out? This article originally appeared on Knoxville News Sentinel: Will Tennessee beat LSU in Lane Kiffin's return to Neyland Stadium? Our pick Tennessee football 's final home game of the 2026 regular season comes with high stakes and a familiar face on the opposing sideline . The No. 9 Vols (8-2, 5-2 SEC) play No. 23 LSU (6-4, 3-4) on Nov. 21 (3:30 p.m. ET, ABC) at Neyland Stadium, welcoming Tigers coach Lane Kiffin back to Knoxville. Kiffin hasn't coached at Neyland Stadium since 2021, when he led Ole Miss and UT fans infamously threw trash on the field, still fueled by anger that Kiffin left Tennessee for USC in 2010. But for all the focus placed on Kiffin, the stakes on the field are as high for Tennessee as they've been for a November home game in years. The Vols are on the verge of a College Football Playoff berth, just needing to win their final two games to make it. At least on paper, this is their toughest game left. Here's what to know about the matchup. Lane Kiffin's first season at LSU has fallen short of expectations Few, if any, coaches generate as much attention as Kiffin. He was the offseason's highest-profile hire after leaving Ole Miss during the College Football Playoff, and the move came with a hefty price tag , including a seven-year contract worth $91 million and a roster budget for 2026 reportedly over $40 million. With that investment comes high expectations, which Kiffin and the Tigers haven't lived up to this fall . It's not like LSU has been getting outclassed by its opponents. Three of its four losses are by one score. But last week's 22-21 loss to Texas dashed any remaining playoff hopes . QB Sam Leavitt has turnover issues but LSU is plenty talented Sam Leavitt was a prized quarterback in the transfer portal coming from Arizona State, however his turnover issues have plagued LSU. He has 12 interceptions, including three against Texas. When Leavitt is on, he is a dynamic quarterback with plenty of weapons at his disposal, like tight end Trey'Dez Green and leading receiver Jackson Harris. The Tigers have the SEC's top passing offense at 316.8 yards per game. Defensively, LSU has one of the most talented groups in the nation. Some players came with Kiffin from Ole Miss, including edge rusher Princewill Umanmielen and linebacker TJ Dottery. Defensive end Jordan Ross transferred from Tennessee and has six sacks, second on the team to Umanmielen (9.5 sacks). The Tigers lead the nation in sacks (40) while Tennessee is second (39). Injuries have piled up for Tennessee this season, and the offense took a major blow when top receiver Mike Matthews suffered a season-ending knee injury against Texas A&M . home.headline: Lane Kiffin just made it clear that he doubts Tennessee fans and their passion for the Vols football program
home.source: A to Z Sports on MSN
home.blurb: LSU Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin just screwed up ahead of a return trip to Neyland Stadium. If you’re a Tennessee fan who’s going to be in Neyland Stadium this weekend for the Vols’ game against LSU, there’s something you need to understand. LSU head coach Lane Kiffin doesn’t believe in you. He doesn’t believe in your ability to create the wildest atmosphere that college football has seen this season. Kiffin, in fact, thinks it’s going to be all good between him and Tennessee fans — the same fans he deserted nearly 17 years ago for one of his many “dream jobs.” The first-year LSU head coach said on Wednesday on the SEC coaches teleconference that he doesn’t think Tennessee fans will be able to create an atmosphere that rivals what he experienced when he returned to Ole Miss earlier this season (another school he deserted). Tennessee has a 59% chance to make the College Football Playoff and a 4% chance to win the national title, according to the A to Z Sports CFB Playoff Predictor (updated November 15, 2026). “I'm not challenging Tennessee, I just don't think you can top that (the Ole Miss atmosphere) from just the feeling of what that was like,” said Kiffin. “Just the anger and hatred because it was so recent that I was in that stadium and that all being there at the start of warm-ups. “And again, I'm not challenging Tennessee. It sounds like I am, but I think once we've gone through that, I think this is more kind of, and it was the last time, this is more kind of fun. They're mad, they're yelling things, they're saying things and it's kind of fun." Well, Lane, you can say what you want, but you’re definitely challenging Vols fans and questioning their passion. Because I promise you, Lane, that Neyland Stadium can get emotionally charged and make you feel the passion of Tennessee fans for four hours unlike anything you’ve ever felt before. Just because you’ve been on the other sideline a few times before doesn’t mean Vols fans are going to take it easy on you or that it won’t affect you. So good luck, Lane. Vols fans don’t need any added motivation, but you just gave them some. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. picks.blurb: Notre Dame Opponent Preview: SMU Mustangs - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games Giannis red hot vs. Bucks Boone's trade charts Cowboys DC latest Story by Roundtable Sports Notre Dame Opponent Preview: SMU Mustangs (Jerome Miron, USA TODAY Sports) Trevor Trowbridge · Roundtable Sports Tue, November 17, 2026 at 10:00 AM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads For the first time since 1989, the Notre Dame Fighting Irish will host the SMU Mustangs inside of Notre Dame Stadium. Their last meeting didn't go too well for the visiting Mustangs as the Irish won 59-6 and took their foot off the gas relatively early in the second half. This year, however, it's a different looking SMU team that travels up north. This program is two years removed from playing for the ACC title and making the first ever 12-team College Football Playoffs. They have talent littered all over the field and will look to play spoiler to Notre Dame's Senior Day and their College Football Playoff hopes. Location : Notre Dame Stadium (Notre Dame, Ind.) Date : Saturday - November 21 Time : 7:30 PM ET TV : NBC/Peacock Line : Notre Dame -20.5; O/U 56.5 Let's kick off our preview of this matchup with an overview look at the SMU Mustangs Record at SMU : 45-19 (5th season) SMU head coach Rhett Lashlee is in the midst of his fifth season at the helm. Like the coach he's facing this Saturday, Marcus Freeman , he has had a winning record in every season he's been the head coach. In 2023 and 2024, the Mustangs posted back to back 11-3 seasons, playing for the ACC title in 2024 and making the College Football Playoffs. Unfortunately, they lost soundly on the road against Penn State but that didn't take away from the great season he had. Last year, expectations were at an all-time high for Lashlee and SMU and they entered as one of the favorites to win the league. Unfortunately, they ended their season at 9-4 and weren't able to handle business down the stretch to get back to the ACC title game.
