home.source: A to Z Sports on MSN
home.blurb: Notre Dame is starting to get some encouraging news on the injury front, and while there are still plenty of questions about who will be available moving forward, the latest developments are reasons for optimism. The biggest news involves offensive lineman Charles Jagusah , who is back practicing with the team this week after a difficult recovery process involving a humerus injury and an infection. There is no definitive timetable for his return to game action, but simply seeing him back on the practice field is a significant step in the right direction. There are also some positive developments on the defensive side, including a potentially important return for star safety Brauntae Johnson . Charles Jagusah's return to practice is a major step It's important not to get ahead of ourselves here. Practicing doesn't mean Jagusah is ready to play, and there isn't a definitive timetable for his return to game action. He still has to work his way back into football shape and demonstrate that he can handle the demands of playing offensive line. Brauntae Johnson could be nearing his return Safety Brauntae Johnson has been upgraded to questionable on the latest availability report ahead of Saturday's matchup against SMU. It's the first time he's appeared in the questionable category after being sidelined with a left foot injury suffered in the season opener against Wisconsin. Freeman previously indicated that Johnson was expected to return sometime in November. Now, with the calendar reaching the second half of the month and Johnson officially listed as questionable, there's legitimate reason to believe his return is getting closer. Left tackle Will Black is listed as questionable after suffering a concussion against Boston College. That's obviously something Notre Dame will need to handle carefully, especially given the importance of his position. Black has been a key part of the offensive line, and his availability is worth watching as the Irish prepare for SMU. The team will need to follow the appropriate concussion protocols before considering a return. On the defensive line, Francis Brewu and Jason Onye remain questionable with knee injuries. Both players have been out since suffering their respective injuries against Navy. Brewu injured his left knee, while Onye is dealing with a right knee injury. That said, seeing both players remain in the questionable category is better than having them ruled out. There's at least some possibility that they're getting closer to returning. Not every player listed above is guaranteed to return this weekend, and Jagusah's situation is still more about long-term progress than an immediate game-day possibility. The Irish don't need to get everybody back this week, but having more healthy bodies available as the season moves toward its most important games would be a welcome development. picks.headline: Missouri Defense Preview: Can Kentucky's offense bounce back?
picks.blurb: Missouri Defense Preview: Can Kentucky's offense bounce back? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games Giannis red hot vs. Bucks Boone's trade charts Cowboys DC latest Story by Wildcats Wire Missouri Defense Preview: Can Kentucky's offense bounce back? Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire · Wildcats Wire Thu, November 19, 2026 at 1:25 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football travels to CoMo for the final road game of the season against the Missouri Tigers. The Wildcats offense desperately needs to respond after scoring just 20 points in the last two weeks which has led to back-to-back losses. Missouri is a well coached, good all around football team and the defense has been consistent this season. However, the Tigers had their worst defensive performance of the season on the road last week against Georgia. Both teams are coming off back-to-back losses, Kentucky has scored just 20 points on offense in the past two weeks. Conversely, the Missouri defense has allowed 72 points over the last two weeks, albeit to Georgia and Texas. Kentucky has to find some of the offensive success they had before the bye week if they want to finish the season on a strong note. A win at Missouri would give the Wildcats six wins in SEC play, which has only happened once in program history and that was in the 1977 season. I fully expect a motivated performance from both teams to try and put an end to their respective two-game losing streaks. Kentucky's offensive line was named a semifinalist for the Joe Moore Award and have since had to of their worst performances of the season. Last week against Florida was the worst the offensive line has looked all season, so you can almost guarantee they will respond the right way in this game. Quiet frankly, they have to because if the offensive line plays like they did against the Gators they will be in danger of a winless month of November. Missouri's defense has playmakers at every level, but they will allow teams to move the football. Among SEC teams, the Tigers rank 10th in success rate allowed, 7th in pass success rate allowed and 12th in rush success rate allowed. Missouri also ranks 8th in the SEC in EPA/play allowed, 7th in EPA/pass allowed and 12th in EPA/rush allowed. The Tigers have also allowed explosive plays this season, as they rank 14th in the conference in explosive play rate allowed. This will be a difficult matchup for Kentucky, but it starts by winning the line of scrimmage and getting the run game going. The Wildcats averaged just two yards per carry against Florida and had just 61 rushing yards. They will lose this game if they can not turn that around, but the Missouri run defense has struggled at times this season. Kentucky has to stay ahead of the chains and that starts with the run game on early downs, which is something they had been good at all season. We mentioned the Tigers have playmakers at every level of the defense, and that starts up front with edge defender Daeden Hopkins. Hopkins leads the team in sacks (7) and tackles for loss (7.5). Linebacker Nicholas Rodriguez leads the middle of the defense, Rodriguez is a tackling machine with a team-leading 107 tackles on the season; he also has seven tackles for loss and 3.5 sacks on the year. The secondary is led by safety Santana Banner, Banner has 84 tackles on the season, 6 pass breakups and 2.5 tackles for loss. Kentucky has to account for these three players, as they are the strength of this Missouri defense at every level. Hopkins, Rodriguez and Banner have each forced two fumbles this season as well. They have consistently made big time plays for the Tigers all season long. Kentucky has to find ways to exploit this defense and avoid letting these three players make game changing plays. In a lot of ways, this matchup is about Kentucky after scoring just 20 points in the last eight quarters. The offense just is not playing well, and what happened on the line of scrimmage against Florida was alarming. Kentucky has to get the big blue wall back to playing like semifinalists for the Joe Moore Award. This offense lacks explosive plays and yards after contact ability, so they will continue to struggle if the offensive line can't get back to playing at a high level. The Tigers have one of the best quarterbacks in the conference, maybe the best duo at wide receiver in the SEC and one of two running backs in the conference that has already rushed for over 1,000 yards. Simmons has thrown for 2,381 passing yards this season and he is constantly pushing the football downfield, his 10.1 average depth of target ranks second in the SEC. He has a 12.3 explosive pass rate, which ranks 4th among SEC quarterbacks. Not to mention, Simmons has been sacked just eight times this season, which is the fewest among starting quarterbacks in the SEC; Simmons doesn't escape sacks like a LaNorris Sellers but he does an incredible job at getting the football out on time. When you look at the advanced stats provided by Clark Brooks of secstatcat.com, these numbers tell a different story that could benefit the Wildcats defense. Simmons is getting a lot of what we would call "turnover luck" this season as he has just three interceptions on the season. However, according to Clark Brooks charting, Simmons has thrown 26 passes this season that could have been intercepted. Kentucky's defense has not forced a turnover after the bye week despite thriving in that area before the bye week, it would be extremely beneficial if the pendulum could swing back in the Wildcats favor in this game and is something to watch. Simmons pushes the football down the field to his top target that also transferred over with him to Missouri from Ole Miss, Cayden Lee. Lee leads the SEC in receptions (65), receiving yards (879) and yards per game (87.9). Lee has five touchdowns on the year and is one of the most dynamic slot receivers in the country. They also have a big playmaker on the outside with Donovan Olugbode, he has 47 catches for 691 yards and 8 touchdowns on the season. Olugbode ranks top six among SEC wide receivers in yards, touchdowns and yards per game. His 6-foot-2, 210-pound frame pairs really well with a dynamic slot receiver like Lee. These are Simmons two go-to guys and he will target his tight ends at times as well. This is one of the most dangerous passing attacks the Wildcats have faced all season, so the secondary will have to play one of their best games of the season in Columbia. Then that brings us to Jamal Roberts, the running back who has filled in for Ahmad Hardy while he was sidelined for a majority of the season. Roberts has been unbelievable as the lead back, he is second in the SEC with 228 carries, 1,133 rushing yards and 113 rushing yards per game. Roberts has 9 rushing touchdowns on the year and he is averaging 4.97 yards per carry. If Roberts is getting the running game going paired with Simmons ability to hit downfield throws, this Tigers offense can be a lot to handle. Missouri is also coming off back-to-back losses to Texas and Georgia, creating a fascinating football game under the lights in CoMo. The Tigers offense struggled last week on the road in Athens and they missed opportunities in the fourth quarter to upset Texas at home the week before. Kentucky's offense has scored just 20 points in the last eight quarters of play. Which offense will show up and bounce back will be the difference in this football game. Nine days ago, Kentucky Football was in the College Football Playoff conversation. Now, the Wildcats are trying to save a season that was turning into something special. The 21-14 loss to Florida on Saturday night at Kroger Field hurt more than most. Kentucky came in as a three-point favorite at home against a 5-4 Gators team. The Cats took a 7-2 lead into halftime and still led 14-13 going into the fourth quarter. Then Florida took over. Aaron Philo ran for 102 yards, the Gators ran for 211 as a team, and Kentucky managed just 61 rushing yards on 27 carries. That’s a season low for a team that came in averaging almost 164 per game. Will Stein didn’t sugarcoat it afterward. He said his team came up short in all three phases. That one stings because of how good this season had been. This was the team that went to College Station and beat No. 9 Texas A&M by 10. It came back from 17 down to win in overtime at South Carolina, beat No. 10 LSU 35-34 in overtime and sent the fans onto the field, then won in Norman. Kentucky was 7-1 and ranked in the top ten of the CFP rankings. Back-to-back losses to Tennessee and Florida later, the playoff dream is just about gone. But there’s still a lot to play for. Kentucky is 7-3 and bowl eligible with two games left: at Missouri and Louisville at home. Win both, then win a bowl game, and Kentucky reaches 10 wins. The program has only done that four times in its history: 1950, 1977, 2018 and 2021. In Stein’s first year, against what his own players called a whole lot of doubt back in August, that would be a remarkable finish. It starts Saturday night in Columbia. Matchup: Kentucky (7-3) at Missouri (6-4, 3-4 SEC) When: Saturday, Nov. 21, 7:30 p.m. ET Where: Faurot Field at Memorial Stadium, Columbia, MO. TV: SEC Network Odds: Missouri -6.5, over/under 50.5 (FanDuel) All-time series: Kentucky leads 9-5 Last meeting: Missouri won 38-21 in Lexington in 2023 Opponent at a Glance: Missouri Tigers Head coach: Eli Drinkwitz (7th season) Missouri started the year ranked No. 25 in the preseason polls. For a while, it looked like the Tigers were exactly who people thought they were. They blew out Florida 45-17, held Texas A&M to six points in a 27-6 win and beat Arkansas by 24. The problem is what happened against good teams. Missouri lost at Mississippi State in September, lost 31-3 at Ole Miss, lost 34-20 at home to Texas and just got rolled 48-21 by No. 1 Georgia in Athens. Two straight losses ended the Tigers’ playoff hopes. The Georgia game was ugly from the first snap. Quarterback Austin Simmons threw an interception on the first play, Georgia scored two plays later, and Missouri was down 31 at halftime. Drinkwitz called it “not a good plan offensively or defensively,” and the Tigers went 2-for-11 on third down. When he gets protection he can pick you apart. RB Ahmad Hardy: A preseason AP First Team All-American and the engine of the run game. Kentucky’s run defense has to be better than it was against Florida. RB Jamal Roberts: The second back in a deep backfield. WR Donovan Olugbode: Simmons’ favorite target and the guy they go to on third down. OL Cayden Green: A preseason Second Team All-American who anchors the line. Keys to the Game Fix the run defense. Florida ran 48 times for 211 yards and wore Kentucky down in the second half. Missouri will try the exact same thing with Hardy. If Kentucky can’t set the edge, it’s going to be a long night. Get the run game going again. Kentucky’s offense works when the run sets up Kenny Minchey. Sixty-one rushing yards won’t win in the SEC, let alone on the road at night. Attack the secondary. Pass defense has been Missouri’s weak spot all year. Georgia’s Gunner Stockton went 18 of 24 for 252 yards. Minchey needs to take his shots. Start fast. Missouri has started slow on the road and on the ropes. Kentucky has led into the second half against Alabama, Tennessee, and Florida and lost all three. The second half is where this team has to grow up. Win the turnover battle. Kentucky’s big wins this year came down to a play here and there. Simmons has been careless with the ball against good defenses. Make him pay. Our Early Prediction This one comes down to which team handles adversity better. Both are coming off back-to-back losses, and both had playoff hopes that are now gone. Missouri has the home field and is favored by almost a touchdown. Kentucky has the head coach who has won close games all year. What gives me some hope is the bounce back. After Alabama blew them out, the Cats went on the road and beat Texas A&M. Stein has had a whole week to get this team’s attention after being called out for not looking like themselves. I think Kentucky responds. All-SEC Georgia star's status in doubt vs. Missouri
home.blurb: However, Georgia has two new players that popped up on the injury report. Georgia starting center Drew Bobo, an All-SEC pick, is doubtful to play. It is unclear what Bobo's injury is, but if he misses the game, then that would be significant for the Georgia offensive line, which is coming off a dominant performance against Ole Miss. Georgia missed Bobo last year in the SEC championship and the postseason. He's a critical part of the Georgia offense. Up front, Georgia's Josh Horton is questionable. Horton is a new player listed on the injury report and has seven tackles and two sacks this season. Pass rusher Amaris Williams remains out for Georgia after tearing his ACL in spring practice. Georgia has some banged up players that aren't on the injury report. Running back Dante Dowdell remains out and running back Chauncey Bowens did not play against Ole Miss despite not having an injury designation. "He's not 100%," Georgia coach Kirby Smart said on Bowens. "Just because someone is dressed out and cleared does not mean that they're able to go out there and play and perform. He's working his tail off to get back." The Tigers are coming off a big loss to the Texas Longhorns, while the Bulldogs just routed the Ole Miss Rebels to propel them to first in the CFP rankings. Drew Bobo is undoubtedly a huge piece to the Bulldogs' offense, as he and QB Gunner Stockton are often on the same page when it comes to play calls and reading the opposing defense. There isn't an injury designation tied to Bobo's absence, but this story will be updated if something surfaces before game time. away.headline: Cal-Stanford Injury Report: Several Key Bears Players Questionable
away.blurb: Cal-Stanford Injury Report: Several Key Bears Players Questionable - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Cal-Stanford Injury Report: Several Key Bears Players Questionable Cal wide receiver Ian Strong is questionable for Saturday | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Jake Curtis · California Golden Bears On SI Thu, November 19, 2026 at 4:36 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Although there are no new Cal players listed as being out, four starters are listed as questionable. Starting wide receiver Ian Strong, who missed last week's game, as well as defensive back Daniel Harris, safety Isaiah Crosby and inside linebacker JD McKinley are the four Cal starters listed as questionable. Safety Aiden Manutai, outside linebacker Justin Beadles and defensive lineman Ashun Shepphard are also Cal players expected to get playing time if they are healthy, but all three are listed as questionable. Also of interest is the fact that quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele and running back Adam Mohammed are listed as probable. That indicates they are likely to play against Stanford, but it also suggests they are nursing some injuries. Three Cal players listed as being out for the Big Game are the same players who have been sidelined for virtually the entire season -- running back Carter Vargas, defensive lineman Nate Burrell and tight end Dorian Thomas. This article was originally published on www.si.com/college/cal as Cal-Stanford Injury Report: Several Key Bears Players Questionable . The initial injury report for Saturday's Cal-Stanford game was released Wednesday night, and a number of key Cal players are listed. Strong is the Bears' second-leading receiver with 35 catches for 478 yards, while McKinley, who also missed last week's game, is the team's co-leader in sacks with three. Crosby is second on the team in tackles with 56 and he also has an interception and two tackles for loss. Harris is fifth on the team in tackles with 37, and he also has three tackles for loss and four quarterback hurries. Cal is 3-7 overall and is riding a four-game losing streak. The Bears will host Stanford (5-5, 4-5 ACC) in Saturday's Big Game starting at 4:30 p.m. The Cardinal would become bowl-eligible if it beats Cal. away.headline: Virginia Tech injury report for Stanford paints a promising outlook for Justin Terry
away.blurb: In the Hokies Week 3 35-26 victory over Maryland, Virginia Tech lost offensive lineman Justin Terry in the first half, and he has been out since then. However, there could be some light at the end of the tunnel for Terry in terms of getting back onto the field, and it might come as soon as this upcoming weekend when Stanford visits . That certainly would be a positive, but a return on Saturday night feels a little ahead of schedule. It would be surprising if he were rushed back from an injury to play against the Cardinal. Franklin said that Terry will likely be a game-time decision. "It's not like we're totally through it," Franklin said. "We still got the rest of the week, and probably will come down to either a game-time decision, or it will be he's cleared, but we still don't feel like he's gotten enough reps." Three regular-season games remain in the 2026 campaign, and already at 6-3, the Hokies are guaranteed a bowl game later next month before the attention shifts toward the 2027 season. Getting Terry back would be a big addition, but even if he does return this weekend, his snaps might be limited; just his presence would be big for Grunkemeyer and the rest of the offense. Virginia Tech football comes out of bye week getting healthier in one pivotal area Going all the way back to the summer, injuries along the offensive line have been an issue for first-year Virginia Tech football coach James Franklin. Then, it carried over into the regular season, where it seems that when it rains, it pours. James Franklin gives positive Justin Terry injury update ahead of Stanford game According to Andy Bitter of Tech Sideline , Terry was going through 1-on-1 drills with the D-linemen. After practice, Franklin gave an update on his linemen ahead of Stanford visiting on Saturday night at Lane Stadium. "So today was really the first day that we've been able to have him for everything," Franklin said , per Virginia Tech Athletics ' YouTube . "We've been kind of working him in slowly. Drills, (individuals), one-on-ones. So today was the first day we've kind of had him for everything. So he's getting closer, and it's positive for us.'' Virginia Tech's offensive line can use all the help it can get If and when Terry comes back, it'll be a welcome sight for Hokies fans. To say that the offensive line has struggled this season would be an understatement. Some of that is because of injuries, while some of it is because there have been guys moved around to different positions. Consistency is key and it feels like there hasn't been much of it this season. Virginia Tech has struggled to protect quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer at times, despite the Penn State transfer having a good year statistically. Then there is the running game that the Hokies have desperately tried to get going. picks.blurb: Utah vs. TCU Prediction, Odds, Injury Report: Week 12 Teams Arizona Wildcats Arizona State Sun Devils Cincinnati Bearcats Colorado Buffaloes Houston Cougars Iowa State Cyclones Kansas Jayhawks Kansas State Wildcats Oklahoma State Cowboys TCU Horned Frogs Texas Tech Red Raiders West Virginia Mountaineers Former Foes Missouri Tigers Nebraska Cornhuskers Oklahoma Sooners Texas A&M Aggies Texas Longhorns Recruiting Football Transfer Portal Video Watch on YouTube Listen on Apple Listen on Spotify Forum Members Login Heartland College Sports – An Independent Big 12 Today Blog | College Football News | Big 12 Today No. 2 Utah heads to Fort Worth on Saturday night with an undefeated season and a spot in the Big 12 Championship Game within reach as the Utes take on TCU in a crucial Week 12 matchup. Utah (10-0, 7-0 Big 12) survived one of the wildest games of the season last weekend, escaping Arizona with a thrilling 40-39 victory. The Utes have now won 10 consecutive games and need just one more victory to secure their place in Arlington. Meanwhile, TCU (5-5, 3-4 Big 12) is coming off a 20-10 victory over Kansas State. The Horned Frogs are one win away from bowl eligibility, but they'll have to earn it against either Utah or Texas Tech in their final two games. Can Utah keep its perfect season alive, or will TCU deliver another Big 12 After Dark surprise? Here's everything you need to know about Utah vs. TCU, including betting odds, injury updates, the biggest question and our prediction. Utah vs. TCU Betting Lines Date: Saturday, November 21, 2026 Kickoff: 8 p.m. CT Location: Amon G. Carter Stadium, Fort Worth, Texas Point Spread: Utah -6.5 Over/Under: 45.5 Odds are from BetMGM on November 17 and are subject to change. Utah vs. TCU Injury Report Utah: Running back Wayshawn Parker was limited against Arizona after dealing with a heel injury. His availability and workload will be worth monitoring heading into Saturday. TCU: This will be updated as needed Biggest Question for Utah vs. TCU: Utah's Run Game vs. TCU's Run Defense The Utah Utes rank third in the Big 12 Conference in rushing yards per game at over 223. But now the Utes hit the road and take on the stingiest run defense in the Big 12, with TCU leading the way in the Big 12 in only allowing 109 rushing yards per game, 10 yards better than anyone else in the conference. How does Devon Dampier, Wayshawn Parker/Daniel Bray handle the ground game, which they will want to get going on the road to stay undefeated? That's the biggest question of the game and will determine whether or not an upset might be in store. Utah vs. TCU Pick and Prediction TCU is 5-5, but every loss has been by one score. That's a testament to this defense, not so much the offense. They have the top scoring defense in the Big 12 this season, and rank second in total defense as well. But here's the thing, TCU's defensive numbers may be skewed in part by who they have, and haven't played, thus far this season. They wrap up the season playing Utah and Texas Tech, two of the more explosive offenses in the Big 12. And the other part of this that concerns me for TCU: Even if the defense holds its own, does it just get worn down as the game progresses, especially if TCU's offense can't get it going? TCU will and can put up an admirable fight, but I don't see it resulting in a win or a cover. Utah is 8-2 against the spread this year, and it'll be 9-2 come Saturday in Fort Worth. The game will be televised nationally on FOX. Where is Utah vs. TCU being played? The game will take place at Amon G. Carter Stadium in Fort Worth, Texas. Who is favored in Utah vs. TCU? Utah is a 6.5-point favorite according to BetMGM's November 17 odds. What does Utah need to reach the Big 12 Championship Game? Utah can secure its spot in the Big 12 Championship Game with a victory over TCU. The Utes enter Week 12 undefeated in conference play at 7-0. Can TCU still become bowl eligible? Yes. away.headline: What's TCU quarterback's status for the showdown with No. 2 Utah?
away.blurb: TCU football is expecting senior quarterback Jaden Craig to be available against No. 2 Utah on Saturday. While Craig will be available on Saturday, it appears he still not be 100% and that means the Horned Frogs could rely on sophomore quarterback Adam Schobel. Schobel played about half a dozen snaps against the Wildcats, rushing for three yards on three carries. “I love Adam; we came in at the same time. He was a freshman when I transferred in,” Pimpton said. “So I have a great relationship with Adam. I’m pretty sure Jay’s going to tough it and play. He’s gonna go out there and do his thing regardless. Whoever goes out there, we will ride behind him no matter what goes on.” Craig was hobbled during TCU’s 20-10 win over Kansas State last Saturday with a lower body injury, but is expected to be a full-go when the Horned Frogs (5-5, 3-4 Big 12) host the Utes (10-0, 7-0) at 8 p.m. on Fox . “I would expect him to play,” TCU head coach Sonny Dykes said Tuesday. “He was a lot better today than he was yesterday, and so I would anticipate him being able to practice tomorrow and play on Saturday. That would be my guess.” If Schobel has to play more against Utah, Dykes doesn’t anticipate the offense needing to change much to fit his skillset. “I think Adam’s a little more mobile than Jaden, and so that would change, but not really,” Dykes said. “The playbook wouldn’t change much. Adam’s been repping our offense all fall camp and all season. So he can go in and execute what we need if we needed him to.” If Schobel gets a bigger role against the Utes, he’ll have the full support of his teammates, like senior tight end Ka’Morreun Pimpton. away.headline: Horned Frogs relishing chance to prove themselves against second-ranked Utes
away.source: The Dallas Morning News on MSN
away.blurb: Quarterback Jaden Craig has been dealing with an ankle injury, but Dykes said he has shown improvement and expects him to be available Saturday. "It's a wonderful opportunity for our team, despite the way the season has been going," Carroll said. "It's such a great opportunity to host No. 2 Utah and go out there and get a W." "Going into a game like that and winning is something you'll never forget," Pimpton said. "We get a chance to go out there and do something amazing by beating the No. 2 team in the nation." FORT WORTH - TCU head coach Sonny Dykes and his players expressed excitement at the challenge of facing No. 2 Utah on Saturday night at Amon G. Carter Stadium. "It's a really good Utah team," Dykes said. "They're No. 2 for a reason. They are good on offense, defense and special teams." In addition to positive words for the Utes, Dykes praised his team's energy during practice and said his players are looking forward to the challenge. "Energy was excellent today," Dykes said. "Guys were excited about practicing. We had a really good day. I think they are excited to play and looking forward to the challenge. They know it's not going to be easy. It's going to take exceptional effort." "I would expect him to play. He was a lot better today than he was yesterday. I would anticipate him being able to practice tomorrow and play on Saturday," Dykes said. Despite the challenges TCU has faced this season, the matchup presents an opportunity for the Horned Frogs to make a statement against one of the nation's top teams.
